chunks: From Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) who said: Indeed, Allah, the Exalted, is not unjust to the servants in the distribution of reward.
But He is unjust to them in the distribution of the deed (work).
ai.seo_question: What is the difference between God's justice in reward and His injustice in the deed?
ai.summary: In *Kamal al-Din*, Shaykh al-Saduq records Imam al-Sadiq’s nuanced distinction between *al-ajr* (reward) and *al-'amal* (the deed itself), clarifying that God’s distribution of the capacity to act is a gratuitous favor (*fadl*) rather than a strict obligation (*wajib*). This theological insight reinforces the Shia doctrine of divine grace, emphasizing that while humans are accountable for their choices, the very ability to choose and act is bestowed by God’s mercy. Such distinctions are pivotal in Shia kalām for resolving apparent contradictions between divine omnipotence and human free will.
